items.stem: Which statement about variable bindings in Rust is correct?

options.text: A binding declared with let is immutable unless mut is added
options.rationale: let bindings are immutable by default; mut opts into mutability.

options.text: All let bindings are mutable by default
options.rationale: Immutability is the default; mut is required to mutate.
Shadowing re-declares with a new let and can change type; mut is not involved.
const must be a compile-time constant with an explicit type and cannot be shadowed in the same way.

items.explanation: let bindings are immutable by default; mut opts into mutability.

items.stem: Select TWO consequences of Rust's ownership move semantics for a non-Copy value such as a String.

options.text: After moving the value, the original variable can no longer be used
options.rationale: A move invalidates the source binding to prevent double frees.

options.text: The value is deep-copied automatically on assignment
options.rationale: Non-Copy types move rather than copy; a deep copy needs an explicit clone().

options.text: Passing it to a function by value transfers ownership into the function
options.rationale: By-value arguments move ownership unless the type is Copy or a reference is passed.

options.text: Borrowing it with & also ends the original binding's validity
options.rationale: A shared borrow does not move the value; the owner remains valid.

items.explanation: A move invalidates the source binding to prevent double frees.

items.stem: What does an Option<T> value let you express that a plain T cannot?

options.text: The explicit possibility that no value is present, checked by the compiler
options.rationale: Option encodes Some/None so absence must be handled, replacing null.

options.text: A value that can be mutated from any thread
options.rationale: Option says nothing about threading or mutability.
That is the role of a plain reference, not Option.

options.text: Automatic error logging when the value is missing
options.rationale: Option carries no logging behaviour of its own.

items.explanation: Option encodes Some/None so absence must be handled, replacing null.
